issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:asymptotic_tracking_vanishing_perturbations is applied to the residual sequence L_t = 1 - a_t b_t with K = [-1,1], but its standing hypothesis that the whole perturbed orbit stays in K is never verified and is false in general: on the certificate level set one only has |L_t| <= 2/delta_t with delta_t < 2 (e.g., the certified scalar point (a,b) = (2,2) at eta = 1/2 has isc(1/2;2,2) = -3/4 < 0 and L_0 = -3), and in the regime delta_t -> 2 the data only give L_t in [-1-o(1), 1+o(1)]. The hypothesis is used essentially: in Step 1 of the lemma's proof, x_{t+1} in U is concluded from |eps_t| < gamma_0 only after invoking x_{t+1} in K, because gamma_0 = dist(f(U-bar cap K), K setminus U) gives no control on the part of R outside K. Symmetric enlargement of K does not fix this either, since g_eta'(1) = (1+eta)^2 > 1 prevents any interval [-1-eps, 1+eps] from being forward invariant. Hence the step 'the proposition yields L_t -> 0' is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote:
We now apply
Proposition~\ref{prop:asymptotic_tracking_vanishing_perturbations}
with $f=g_\eta$, $K=[-1,1]$, $\Lambda=\{0\}$, and
$t_\ast := t_k + N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma using the strictly invariant neighborhood already produced in the application: since U is shrunk so that its closure lies in (-1,1) and |g_eta'| <= q < 1 there, one has g_eta(U-bar) compactly contained in U, so redefine gamma_0 := dist(g_eta(U-bar), R setminus U) > 0 and drop the global (x_t) subset K requirement, running Steps 1-3 on the compact set U-bar; correspondingly extend the finite-horizon tracking estimate used in the entry step to a fixed compact interval containing the bounded sequences. All theorem statements are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence proof for the terminal regime delta_* = 2 with eta in (0,1) has a gap: the delta_t -> 2 case of Theorem thm:convergence_region_rank_1 (1), the scalar convergence recovery of Section subsec:scalar_factorization, and the delta_t -> 2 case (convergence to the minimizer set) of Theorem thm:convergence_region_rank_1_approx all rest on an unverified, generally false hypothesis of the perturbation lemma.
issues.title: Perturbation lemma applied to the residual sequence L_t without verifying its standing hypothesis that the orbit remain in K = [-1,1]
issues.why_classification: The needed strict invariance and positive margin are already established in the text, so the fix is a local restatement of the lemma's margin definition plus a routine extension of the tracking estimate by uniform continuity on a compact interval; every claim, regime, and guarantee survives unchanged and no new nontrivial lemma, construction, or global argument is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For every $\delta \in [\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta), \overline\delta)$ and every
    $x \in \RR^2$ with $I(\delta;\,x) = 0$, equality holds in
    Axiom~\ref{cond:monotonicity} if and only if $\nabla \risk(x) = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark asserts that the normalized scalar certificate satisfies Axioms A1-A7 with threshold delta_th(eta) = eta. Axiom A6 fails at delta = eta: the paper's own recursion gives isc(eta; gd_eta(x)) = R^sc(eta) = eta(eta-eta)(eta^2-4)L^2 = 0 for every x on the level set {isc(eta) = 0}, so equality in A5 holds at every boundary point, not only at stationary points. Concretely, for eta = 1/2 the non-stationary point (sqrt(5), sqrt(5)) lies on {isc(1/2) = 0} and is mapped to (-sqrt(5), -sqrt(5)), still on the same level set, so equality in A5 holds at a point with nonzero gradient, violating the 'if and only if' in A6. What is actually true is that A1-A7 hold with any threshold delta_th in (eta, 2): for delta > eta the remainder is strictly negative away from the stationary set.

failure_location.quote:
One verifies directly that Axioms~\ref{cond:P_is_pd}--\ref{cond:symmetry} hold
with $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta) = \eta$ when $\eta <2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'delta_th(eta) = eta' by 'any delta_th(eta) in (eta, 2)' (A5 and A6 hold on (eta,2) and A6 fails at the endpoint); wherever a range [delta_th(eta), 2) is used, take the threshold arbitrarily close to eta.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed sharp threshold delta_th(eta) = eta for the axiom system is incorrect; the framework applies to the scalar certificate only on the open range delta in (eta, 2). Downstream impact is nil: the uniqueness proof is carried out at fixed delta strictly above the threshold, and the initializations with state parameter exactly eta form the measure-zero boundary {isc(eta) = 0}, which the almost-everywhere statements exclude anyway.
issues.title: Claim that the scalar certificate satisfies Axioms A1-A7 with threshold delta_th(eta) = eta is false: Axiom A6 (stationarity) fails at the endpoint delta = eta
issues.why_classification: The correction is a one-line weakening of the threshold claim that preserves every subsequent use: the uniqueness argument works at delta strictly above the threshold, and the only states at exactly eta form a measure-zero set excluded from the almost-everywhere results; no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Thus the unbalanced minimizers sweep out the full
nonterminal parameter range $(0,2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lagrange computation proves: whenever a nonterminal level set {I(delta;x) = 0} contains an unbalanced minimizer x_* = (a_*, 1/a_*), the matrix on that level set equals the displayed formula evaluated at delta' := 4a_*^2/(a_*^4+1). But the theorem asserts that the family's own state parameter delta equals this derived delta'. Every axiom A1-A7 involves delta only through the nested sublevel sets K_delta and is therefore invariant under increasing reparametrizations of the state: for any increasing homeomorphism phi of (0,2] with phi(2) = 2 and phi not the identity, the family P-tilde(delta) := P_std(phi(delta)) satisfies A1-A7 with the same level sets and threshold phi^{-1}(eta), yet differs from the displayed 'unique' P(delta). Hence the claimed parameterized uniqueness is false; the axioms determine at most the nested level-set family up to reparametrization. Additionally, the coverage step 'the unbalanced minimizers sweep out the full nonterminal parameter range (0,2)' is circular: it presupposes the identification of the family's parameter with the derived one, and no argument is given that every nonterminal level set contains an unbalanced minimizer.

failure_location.quote:

$\delta \in [\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta), \overline\delta)$. With state space
$(0, 2]$, the unique family is

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to: the nested family of sublevel sets is uniquely determined by the axioms, so any admissible family has the form P_std(phi(delta)) for an increasing homeomorphism phi of (0,2] fixing 2, with the displayed P(delta) as the canonical representative determined by delta = 4a_*^2/(a_*^4+1); and supply the missing coverage argument - a nonterminal level set containing no unbalanced minimizer would be an ellipsoid with nonempty interior strictly contained in every minimizer-carrying (standard) level set, hence in their intersection K_2, which has empty interior, a contradiction (a sandwiching argument between consecutive standard ellipses forces each level set to equal a standard one). Qualify the dependent prose and rmk:ext_to_quartic accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness theorem as stated is false; the provable content is uniqueness of the nested level-set family up to increasing reparametrization of delta, with the displayed formula as a canonical representative. The same qualification is needed for the quartic-loss extension asserted in rmk:ext_to_quartic and for the prose claims (abstract, contributions, conclusion) that 'the scalar certificate is uniquely determined'. The block-structure propositions prop:diag10_structure and prop:diag1sigma_structure use only the level-set content and are unaffected.
issues.title: Uniqueness of the parameterized family P(delta) is false as stated: the axioms are invariant under reparametrization of the state, and the coverage step is circular
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening of the uniqueness notion (level sets unique up to relabeling of the state, rather than the parameterized matrix being unique) plus a contained nontrivial coverage argument; the conceptual contribution - the certificate's geometry is forced by the monotonicity axioms rather than guessed - survives in recognizably comparable form, so no central result is abandoned and no new global proof architecture is needed, but the change is more than a short local fix.
